title: Processing of identified homeowner data during registration
description: During account registration, the Homeowner provides identified personal data (name, email, contact information) which is processed by the Home Hub. This creates a direct link between the data subject and their personal information.
assumptions: Registration requires personal identification information

title: Unique identifiers in registration and device enrollment
description: The registration process creates unique identifiers (account ID, email) and device enrollment creates unique device identifiers that serve as direct references to the homeowner's identity.
assumptions: System assigns unique IDs to accounts and enrolled devices

title: Linking through unique identifiers across registration and device data
description: The Home Hub can link registration data with enrolled camera/sensor data through unique identifiers, creating a comprehensive profile of the homeowner and their devices.
assumptions: System maintains relationships between account and device data

title: Profiling through device enrollment patterns
description: The combination of account registration data and enrolled devices (cameras/sensors) enables profiling of the homeowner's security preferences, home layout, and lifestyle patterns.
assumptions: Device types and placement patterns can reveal personal information

title: Potentially excessive data collection during registration
description: The registration process may collect more sensitive personal data than functionally required for basic account creation and device enrollment.
assumptions: Registration form may include optional or unnecessary fields
uncertainty_note: Depends on specific registration form design

title: Data retention beyond functional necessity
description: Registration and device enrollment data may be retained longer than needed for the functional purpose of account management and device operation.
assumptions: No explicit retention policy or data deletion mechanism

title: Unawareness of data processing scope
description: The Homeowner may not be fully aware of all personal data being collected, how it will be processed, or what inferences can be drawn from device enrollment patterns.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not fully disclose all processing activities

title: Limited control over data processing preferences
description: The Homeowner may lack granular control over which data is collected during registration and how device enrollment data is processed.
assumptions: Registration may use all-or-nothing consent model

title: Attributable registration and enrollment data
description: Registration records and device enrollment data create attributable evidence that can prevent the homeowner from denying their account creation or device enrollment actions.
assumptions: System maintains audit logs of registration and enrollment events

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: If the registration process collects more personal data than necessary for account creation and device enrollment, this may violate GDPR data minimization requirements.
assumptions: Registration may include unnecessary data fields
uncertainty_note: Depends on specific data collection practices

title: Access code entry creates attributable evidence
description: When a guest enters a temporary access code at the Home Hub, the system may log this action. This log entry can be used to attribute the door unlock action to a specific guest, preventing them from denying they accessed the property.
assumptions: The Home Hub maintains access logs that record when access codes are entered and which door was unlocked.

title: Access code is sensitive data
description: The temporary access code is sensitive authentication data. If this code is logged, stored, or transmitted beyond what is necessary for the immediate door unlock function, it represents unnecessary collection of sensitive data.
assumptions: The access code may be stored or logged by the Home Hub beyond the immediate authentication process.

title: Access code retention duration unclear
description: If the Home Hub logs access code entries, the duration for which this data is retained may exceed what is functionally necessary for door access control, potentially violating data minimization principles.
assumptions: The system may retain access logs longer than needed for the immediate access control function.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain about actual retention policies of the Home Hub system.

title: Guest unaware of data processing
description: The guest entering the access code may not be aware that their access attempt is being logged, recorded, or processed by the Home Hub system beyond the immediate door unlock function.
assumptions: Guests are not informed about what data is collected when they use temporary access codes.

title: Guest lacks control over access data processing
description: The guest has no ability to set preferences or provide consent regarding how their access data (time, location, code entry) is processed, stored, or shared by the Home Hub system.
assumptions: The system does not provide guests with options to control their data processing preferences.

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: If the Home Hub collects and stores more data than necessary for the door unlock function (e.g., logging access codes, timestamps, or guest identifiers), this may violate GDPR's data minimization principle.
assumptions: The system may process more personal data than strictly required for the access control functionality.
uncertainty_note: Depends on actual data collection practices of the Home Hub.

title: Motion pattern profiling
description: Real-time motion alerts from the Home Hub can be analyzed to profile individual behavior patterns, such as daily routines, presence/absence schedules, and activity patterns within the home.
assumptions: Motion data includes timestamp and potentially location/sensor information that enables pattern analysis

title: Revealing presence attributes
description: Motion alert data contains revealing attributes that can identify when individuals are present or absent from the home, potentially exposing sensitive information about occupancy patterns.
assumptions: Motion alerts are generated based on human movement detection

title: Sensitive motion data collection
description: Motion data is highly sensitive as it reveals presence/absence and activity patterns. Collecting real-time motion alerts may exceed what is functionally required for basic alert functionality.
assumptions: Motion data reveals intimate details about home occupancy and routines

title: Excessive data granularity
description: Real-time motion alerts provide fine-grained temporal data about movement, which is more granular than needed for simple notification purposes.
assumptions: Alerts include precise timing of motion events

title: Implicit presence disclosure
description: Motion alerts implicitly disclose presence/absence information as a side-effect of the explicit motion detection functionality, revealing when the home is occupied.
assumptions: Motion detection inherently reveals occupancy status

title: Unawareness of motion data processing
description: Data subjects may not be fully aware that their motion patterns are being collected, processed, and transmitted to the mobile app backend in real-time.
assumptions: Users may not understand the extent of motion data collection

title: Lack of motion data preferences
description: Data subjects may lack control to set preferences or consent regarding how motion data is collected, processed, and transmitted to the backend.
assumptions: Motion data collection settings may not be configurable by users

title: Data minimization violation
description: Collecting and transmitting real-time motion alerts may violate the data minimization principle if less granular or less frequent data would suffice for the intended functionality.
assumptions: Real-time motion data may be more than necessary for alert purposes
uncertainty_note: Depends on specific functional requirements of the alert system

title: Profiling through motion detection patterns
description: Motion detection notifications can reveal patterns about when the homeowner is present or absent from their property. Over time, this data can be analyzed to profile the homeowner's daily routines, travel patterns, and occupancy habits.
assumptions: The backend stores or processes motion detection events that can be correlated over time

title: Processing of identified homeowner data
description: The mobile app backend processes identified data to route motion detection notifications to the specific homeowner's device. This requires maintaining and using personal identifiers.
assumptions: The system uses user identifiers to deliver notifications to the correct homeowner

title: Detection through observed communications
description: The notification communications themselves reveal that motion detection is active and when motion events occur. An observer monitoring communications could detect these patterns.
assumptions: Communication channels could be monitored by third parties

title: Sensitive occupancy data disclosure
description: Motion detection notifications disclose sensitive information about property occupancy patterns, which could be considered more sensitive than functionally required for simple notification purposes.
assumptions: Motion detection data reveals occupancy patterns that may be more sensitive than needed

title: Lack of homeowner control over notification preferences
description: The homeowner may lack sufficient control to customize which motion detection events trigger notifications, how frequently they receive them, or what information is included in notifications.
assumptions: The system may not provide granular notification preference controls

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: If the notification includes more data than necessary (e.g., exact timestamps, location details, or motion intensity) beyond what is needed to alert the homeowner, this could violate data minimization requirements.
assumptions: The notification may contain more granular data than functionally required
uncertainty_note: Depends on actual notification content implementation

title: Data shared with predetermined external party
description: Aggregated device-usage analytics are shared with a cloud analytics vendor (EE3), a predetermined external party. This exposes personal data to a third party beyond the mobile app backend's direct control.
assumptions: The cloud analytics vendor is a known, fixed party in the system architecture

title: Data propagation to external service
description: Device-usage analytics data is propagated to an external cloud analytics vendor where it may be processed, stored, or further shared beyond the original functional scope of the mobile app.
assumptions: The analytics vendor may use the data for purposes beyond what the mobile app backend requires

title: Profiling through device usage analytics
description: Aggregated device-usage analytics can be analyzed to identify patterns and profile individual users based on their device behavior, even if the data is labeled as aggregated.
assumptions: Analytics data contains sufficient detail to enable behavioral profiling
uncertainty_note: Depends on the granularity of the aggregated data

title: Quasi-identifiers in analytics data
description: Device-usage analytics may contain combinations of attributes (e.g., device type, usage patterns, timestamps) that serve as quasi-identifiers, potentially allowing re-identification of individuals.
assumptions: The aggregated analytics retain enough attribute detail to enable quasi-identification
uncertainty_note: Depends on the level of aggregation and anonymization applied

title: User unawareness of analytics sharing
description: Data subjects may not be aware that their device-usage analytics are being shared with an external cloud analytics vendor, especially if this is not clearly disclosed in privacy notices.
assumptions: Privacy disclosures may not clearly communicate third-party analytics sharing

title: Lack of user control over analytics processing
description: Users may lack the ability to set preferences or provide consent regarding how their device-usage analytics are processed and shared with the cloud analytics vendor.
assumptions: The system may not provide granular consent options for analytics sharing

title: Potential violation of data minimization
description: Sharing aggregated device-usage analytics with an external vendor may process more personal data than is functionally necessary for the mobile app's core functionality.
assumptions: Analytics sharing may not be strictly required for the app's primary purpose
uncertainty_note: Depends on whether analytics are essential to app functionality

title: Invalid consent for analytics sharing
description: If users have not provided valid, informed consent for sharing device-usage analytics with the cloud analytics vendor, this constitutes unlawful processing under GDPR.
assumptions: Consent mechanisms may not be properly implemented or may be bundled with other terms
uncertainty_note: Depends on the actual consent implementation in the mobile app

title: Video data contains sensitive personal information
description: Video clips stored in cloud storage may contain highly sensitive personal data (faces, activities, property details) that exceeds what is functionally required for simple playback functionality.
assumptions: Video content includes identifiable personal information about homeowners and their property

title: Video data accessible to mobile app backend
description: Personal video data is made accessible to the mobile app backend process, which may be more parties than functionally necessary for the playback functionality.
assumptions: The mobile app backend is a separate system component that processes video data

title: Video content reveals identifying attributes
description: Video clips may contain revealing attributes (faces, license plates, distinctive features) that support identification of data subjects beyond what is needed for playback.
assumptions: Video content includes visual information that can identify individuals

title: Video playback patterns enable individual profiling
description: Analysis of which video clips are retrieved and when can be used to profile homeowner behavior and patterns, linking data to specific individuals.
assumptions: Video retrieval metadata is logged and can be analyzed for patterns

title: Homeowners unaware of video processing details
description: Data subjects (homeowners) may not be fully aware of how their video data is being processed, stored, and retrieved by the mobile app backend.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not clearly explain video data processing flows

title: Limited control over video data retention and deletion
description: Homeowners may lack control to rectify or erase video data that is no longer relevant, particularly regarding retention periods in cloud storage.
assumptions: Video deletion/retention controls may not be user-configurable

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: Processing full video clips may violate GDPR data minimization if less granular data (e.g., thumbnails, metadata only) could achieve the same playback functionality.
assumptions: Full video retrieval is required for playback functionality
uncertainty_note: Depends on whether video content is strictly necessary for the stated functionality

title: Insufficient data subject controls for video data
description: GDPR requires data subject rights including access, rectification, and erasure which may not be adequately supported for video data in this flow.
assumptions: Video data management may not include comprehensive data subject rights mechanisms
